topic: Swallow screening within 4 hours of stroke

audits.title: 79 Aiming to be champions: stroke swallow screen audit
audits.standard: Stroke swallow screen completed within 4 hours of presentation (National Stroke Guidelines 2022)

cycle1.result: 44% (39 patients) had a swallow screen; only 13% (11 patients) within 4 hours.

audits.intervention: Planned: SLT-led training of relevant staff and a swallow screen QI programme for 2023.
audits.other_findings: National figures quoted for 2022 were 70% screened and 43% within 4 hours.
audits.citation: Ward C, Johnston A, Cheannabhain A, Diskin M, Hannon N. 79 Aiming to be champions: stroke swallow screen audit. Age and Ageing. 2023;52(Supplement_3). doi:10.1093/ageing/afad156.097.

audits.title: 91 Audit of percentage of stroke patients having swallow screen performed within 4 hrs of diagnosis on the stroke ward in OLOL Hospital Drogheda
audits.standard: HSE National Guideline for Swallow Screening 2017: swallow screen within 4 hours of diagnosis
audits.setting: Level 3 stroke ward, Our Lady of Lourdes Hospital, Drogheda

cycle1.result: 24 of 29 had a documented swallow assessment; only 3 were screened within 4 hours of diagnosis.

audits.intervention: Planned: teaching sessions and reminder charts for on-call NCHDs and nursing staff.
audits.citation: Clancy C. 91 Audit of percentage of stroke patients having swallow screen performed within 4 hrs of diagnosis on the stroke ward in OLOL Hospital Drogheda. Age and Ageing. 2023;52(Supplement_3). doi:10.1093/ageing/afad156.106.

audits.title: 254 An Audit of the Frequency of Early Swallow Screens Performed in Patients Diagnosed with a Stroke
audits.standard: RCP Stroke Guidelines 2016 and National Guideline for Swallow Screening in Stroke (2017): swallow screen within 4 hours of admission
audits.setting: Stroke service, Mayo University Hospital, Castlebar

cycle1.result: 38 (48.1%) had a documented swallow screen during admission, 27 (34.2%) did not, 14 (17.7%) unclear; 5 of 38 (13.2%) within 4 hours.

audits.intervention: Planned education and training programme for stroke unit nurses and doctors, with re-audit in 6–12 months.
audits.other_findings: Over 90% of stroke patients were admitted to the stroke unit.
audits.citation: Kelly L, Murtagh N, Leonard R, O'Malley T. 254 An Audit of the Frequency of Early Swallow Screens Performed in Patients Diagnosed with a Stroke. Age and Ageing. 2019;48(Supplement_3):iii17-iii65. doi:10.1093/ageing/afz103.156.

audits.title: Full Implementation of Screening for Nutritional Risk and Dysphagia in an Acute Stroke Unit: A Clinical Audit.
audits.standard: National guideline for nutritional risk and dysphagia screening in acute stroke (introduced 1 June 2012)
audits.setting: Acute stroke unit, University Hospital of North Norway

cycle1.result: Nutritional risk screening performed in 65% and swallow testing in 91% of eligible patients.

audits.intervention: Clinical microsystems approach with rapid improvement cycles and audits over 6 months.
audits.other_findings: Nutritional risk prevalence 29%; 23% failed the initial swallow test.
audits.citation: Kampman MT, Eltoft A, Karaliute M, Børvik MT, Nilssen H, Rasmussen I, et al.. Full Implementation of Screening for Nutritional Risk and Dysphagia in an Acute Stroke Unit: A Clinical Audit. Neurohospitalist. 2015;5(4):205-211. doi:10.1177/1941874415588749. PMID: 27733895.

audits.title: Dysphagia screening after acute stroke: a quality improvement project using criteria-based clinical audit.
audits.standard: Evidence-based recommendation to screen for swallowing deficit with a standardised tool
audits.setting: Small stroke unit, Haukeland University Hospital

cycle1.result: Complete swallow screening documented in 6% (95% CI 2-11).

audits.intervention: Workshops, local opinion leaders, manual paper reminders and feedback, informed by root-cause analysis.
audits.citation: Sivertsen J, Graverholt B, Espehaug B. Dysphagia screening after acute stroke: a quality improvement project using criteria-based clinical audit. BMC Nurs. 2017;16:27. doi:10.1186/s12912-017-0222-6. PMID: 28588423.

audits.title: Swallow evaluation tool to reduce aspiration among acute stroke patients: A quality improvement project.
audits.standard: Dysphagia screening with a validated tool (Yale Swallow Protocol) within 24 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Aspiration incidence 42.5% among acute stroke patients; existing screening tool not validated.

audits.intervention: Yale Swallow Protocol added to the nurses' admission bundle with SLP referral on failure, plus nurse education and weekly audits.

cycle2.result: 37 of 63 (59%) screened within 24 h of admission; 3 of 37 screened had aspiration pneumonia.

audits.other_findings: Overall compliance with using the tool was 59%.
audits.citation: Koirala E, Greely C, Fitzpatrick S. Swallow evaluation tool to reduce aspiration among acute stroke patients: A quality improvement project. J Vasc Nurs. 2025;43(1):1-9. doi:10.1016/j.jvn.2024.11.001. PMID: 40057346.
